listeners.why: Each of these is a callback for something the Electron main process pushes: a task switched from the tray menu, an OAuth redirect caught on a loopback port, a request to the local REST API. This port has no main process and starts none of those, so each member records the callback and never fires it.

noop.why: Messages the renderer sends so that the Electron main process can update something outside the page: the tray and its tooltip, the task widget window, global shortcuts, the taskbar progress bar, the title bar overlay, the window-close hooks, the settings copy main keeps. There is no second process and none of those surfaces exist here, so there is nothing to tell and nothing to disagree with. `on(channel, listener)` is the generic subscription to the events main pushes (idle time, tray clicks, global shortcuts, app-URI actions): none of them is ever sent. `openDevTools` is the global error handler's offer to open the developer tools after an error, called from inside that handler: a refusal there would be a second error, and the first one is already in the console.

getDistChannel.why: upstream's own answer on a platform it cannot classify (electron/shared-with-frontend/get-dist-channel.ts). The renderer then labels the build 'web', appends no channel suffix to its version string and does not treat the build as store-updated.

isGnomeDesktop.why: Read only by plugins (app.constants.ts says so). The page does not know the desktop environment.

isGnomeWayland.why: Upstream uses it for exactly one decision: drawing its own title bar. false leaves that decision at the app's own default.

isMacOS.why: The renderer's macOS branch assumes Electron's hidden-inset traffic lights over its own header. A browser tab has none, on any host, so the non-macOS layout is the right one everywhere.

isAppleSilicon.why: A page cannot tell; app.constants.ts says the web build stays false for the same reason.

isSnap.why: This is not a Snap package. true would route file saves through a native dialog this port refuses.

isFlatpak.why: This is not a Flatpak package.

getPathForFile.why: webUtils.getPathForFile returns a host path for a dropped file, and Orivon never gives a page one. null is what the renderer already handles: it falls back to the file's name (drop-paste-input.ts).

consumeJiraApi.why: Jira requests are made by the Electron main process with Node's HTTP stack. null is the renderer's own 'unavailable' answer (jira-electron-bridge.service.ts): a Jira request then rejects with 'Jira Electron API is unavailable' instead of reaching a server.

consumePluginNodeExecutionApi.why: Plugins that run Node scripts need a Node process. null is the preload's own answer once the one-shot API has been taken, and plugin-bridge.service.ts treats it as 'plugin Node execution unavailable'.

checkBackupAvailable.why: Upstream's answer when no automatic backup file exists. This port writes none (see backupAppData), so there is never one to offer at start-up.

listBackups.why: No automatic backup files exist, so the restore-from-backup list is empty.

backupAppData.why: The Electron app writes a JSON backup into its user-data folder every few minutes. This port holds no such folder and asks for no file access, so no backup is written; a resolved call keeps the backup service from logging a failure every interval. Export (Settings, Import/Export) and sync are the ways to get a copy out.

getSyncFolderPath.why: upstream's answer when no local sync folder is configured, which is always the case here.

commitPickedDirectory.why: upstream's answer for a routine save without a pick, which is always the case here since pickDirectory is refused.

discardPickedDirectory.why: Nothing is ever pending. The caller chains .catch() on the result, so this must return a promise, not undefined.

imageCacheGetDataUrl.why: upstream's answer for an unknown id, so a background image that was never imported renders as none. Importing one is refused (imagePickAndImport).

getClipboardFilePaths.why: The clipboard's file paths are host paths. [] is the answer for 'no file on the clipboard', and the renderer then reads the image from the paste event itself.

readClipboardImage.why: The Electron clipboard is not reachable from a page. null is 'no image on the clipboard' and sends the renderer on to the image in the paste event.

copyClipboardImageFile.why: Copies a host file into the images folder. A page holds no host file path, so there is never a file to copy; null is upstream's 'nothing copied'.

getClipboardImagePath.why: The host path of a saved image. null is upstream's 'no such image'.

relaunch.why: The browser owns the app's lifetime. Reached after a setting that asks for a restart.

exit.why: Closing is the tab's, not the app's.

shutdownNow.why: Shutting down the computer is a power Orivon does not have. Reached only from the daily summary's shutdown button.

lockScreen.why: Locking the operating-system session is a power Orivon does not have. Reached only from the take-a-break feature's lock-screen option.

openPath.why: Opens a file or folder on the computer in its default program. Orivon gives a page no host paths to open.

shareNative.why: The operating system's share sheet is not reachable from a page.

saveFileDialog.why: Reached only when the app believes it runs as a Snap package, which it does not here. Saving a file is the browser's download.

showOpenDialog.why: Returns a host folder path for the clipboard-images setting. Orivon hands a page opaque handles, never path strings.

getUserDataPath.why: Returns the host path of the app's data folder. Read only to build the default clipboard-images folder.

loadBackupData.why: Reads a backup file chosen from listBackups, which is always empty.

fileSyncSave.why: Local-folder sync writes into a folder the user picked. Not built in this port; sync through WebDAV or the app's own sync server instead.

fileSyncLoad.why: The read half of local-folder sync; see fileSyncSave.

fileSyncRemove.why: The delete half of local-folder sync; see fileSyncSave.

checkDirExists.why: Checks the local sync folder; see fileSyncSave.

pickDirectory.why: Picks the local sync folder; see fileSyncSave. Reached from the sync settings when the local-folder provider is chosen.

imagePickAndImport.why: Imports a background image into a cache folder owned by the main process. Reached from the theme settings.

saveClipboardImage.why: Writes a pasted image into a folder on disk. Not built in this port.

loadClipboardImage.why: Reads a pasted image back from that folder.

deleteClipboardImage.why: Deletes a pasted image from that folder.

listClipboardImages.why: Lists the images in that folder.

pluginOAuthPrepare.why: Starts a loopback HTTP listener in the main process to catch an OAuth redirect for a plugin.

pluginOAuthStart.why: Opens the system browser on the OAuth URL and waits for the listener started by pluginOAuthPrepare.

getLocalRestApiToken.why: The local REST API is a server the main process runs on a loopback port. This port starts none, so there is no token; the settings field shows its own error state.
